----------------------------------------------------------------
EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN
----------------------------------------------------------------

1. Identification Strategy
----------------------------------------------------------------
Chosen method: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD).

Justification
• Eligibility for Canadian social assistance is a deterministic, one-shot rule based on a continuous running variable (pre-benefit income) and a known cutoff.  
• Individuals immediately below and above the cutoff are plausibly comparable except for treatment status, satisfying the core RDD intuition of “as-good-as-random” assignment in a neighborhood of the threshold.  
• Monthly panel data let us estimate both contemporaneous and dynamic treatment effects by stacking outcomes at different post-eligibility horizons in an RD-event-study framework.  
• Unlike DiD, RDD does not require parallel-trend assumptions; unlike IV, it does not rely on exclusion restrictions—the discontinuity itself provides the source of quasi-random variation.

2. Treatment and Control
----------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
Treated = 1 if the individual’s pre-determination monthly income y_i,t falls strictly below the statutory cutoff c in month t, making the person eligible and actually receiving social assistance in t+1 (sharp design). Treated = 0 otherwise.

Control group  
Individuals with income just above the cutoff (y_i,t ≥ c) in the same local bandwidth who therefore do not receive assistance.

Running variable and cutoff  
Running variable R_i,t = y_i,t − c.  
Cutoff at R = 0. We will pool observations from all provinces but allow province-specific cutoffs; in practice we center income within each province/year and stack the data.

Treatment timing / event date  
t = 0 is the month eligibility is determined. Outcomes are observed at horizons k = 0, 1, 3, 6, 12 months post-eligibility.

3. Key Identifying Assumptions
----------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Continuity of potential outcomes: In the absence of treatment, employment and income would evolve smoothly through the cutoff.  
 Plausibility: There is no other policy kink at exactly the same income level; demographic covariates should look balanced.

A2. No precise manipulation of the running variable: Individuals cannot perfectly position their reported income just below the cutoff.  
 Plausibility: Monthly income is largely determined by payroll withholding; we will test using the McCrary density test.

A3. Local stable unit treatment value (SUTVA): Treatment of one individual does not directly affect close-threshold neighbors within the bandwidth.  
 Plausibility: Spillovers in labor markets at this micro scale are negligible.

A4. Consistent treatment: Crossing the threshold induces full benefit take-up (sharp design).  
 Plausibility: Administrative rules automatically enroll eligible individuals; we will verify actual receipt rates.

4. Threats to Identification and Mitigation
----------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Income manipulation/bunching  
  • Test: McCrary density, donut RD removing ±$50 around cutoff.  
  • Mitigation: If bunching detected, re-specify as fuzzy RD, instrumenting receipt with eligibility.

T2. Differential covariate patterns  
  • Test: RD estimates on baseline covariates (age, gender, education).  
  • Mitigation: Include those covariates in the RD; use covariate-adjusted rdrobust.

T3. Heterogeneous provincial rules (multiple cutoffs)  
  • Mitigation: Estimate province-specific RDs, then aggregate via inverse-variance weights; include province-month fixed effects in stacked design.

5. R Code Outline
----------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# ---- Packages ----
library(data.table)   # fast data handling
library(rdrobust)     # RD estimation
library(fixest)       # high-dimensional FE regressions
library(ggplot2)

# ---- 1. Load data ----
dt <- fread("can_sa_admin.csv")   # assume month-level panel

# ---- 2. Variable construction ----
# Center income around province-specific cutoff
dt[, R := income - cutoff_income]        # running variable
dt[, treat := as.integer(R < 0)]         # treatment indicator

# Define outcomes at several horizons
setkey(dt, id, month)
for(k in c(0,1,3,6,12)){
  dt[, paste0("empl_p",k) := shift(employed, -k, type="lead"), by = id]
  dt[, paste0("earn_p",k) := shift(labor_income, -k, type="lead"), by = id]
}

# ---- 3. Main RD specification (6-month horizon) ----
bw <- rdrobust::rdbwselect(y = dt$empl_p6, x = dt$R)$bws[1,1]

rd_main <- rdrobust(y = dt$empl_p6,
                    x = dt$R,
                    c = 0,
                    h = bw,
                    p = 1,            # local linear
                    covs = as.matrix(dt[, .(age, female, educ_yrs)]))

summary(rd_main)

# ---- 4. Dynamic RD-event-study plot ----
out_horizons <- lapply(c(0,1,3,6,12), function(k){
  rdrobust(y = dt[[paste0("empl_p",k)]], x = dt$R, h = bw)$coef[1]
})
plot_df <- data.frame(k=c(0,1,3,6,12), tau=unlist(out_horizons))
ggplot(plot_df, aes(k, tau)) + geom_line() + geom_point() +
  ylab("RD treatment effect on employment") + xlab("Months after eligibility")

# ---- 5. Robustness check: narrower bandwidth ----
rd_rb <- rdrobust(y = dt$empl_p6, x = dt$R, h = bw/2, p = 1)
summary(rd_rb)
```

6. Expected Results
----------------------------------------------------------------
Theory (labor-supply disincentive) predicts:
• Employment probability: 5–10 pp reduction within six months for those just made eligible.  
• Total income: small positive or zero change (transfer offsets reduced labor earnings).  
Magnitude: τ_empl ≈ −0.07 (SE ≈ 0.02); τ_income ≈ +$150/month (SE ≈ $75).

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (0/1)
----------------------------------------------------------------
C1. Smooth density of running variable at cutoff………. 1  
C2. Covariate balance across cutoff………………………………… 1  
C3. Correct functional form / bandwidth choice……………… 0.5 (always debatable)  
C4. No other policy change at cutoff……………………………… 1  
C5. Stable treatment definition & take-up……………………… 1  

Overall score: 4.5 / 5 → design appears credible but still contingent on diagnostics.
